Container.Name: PhotoBrowser

Branch.TagDescription: Latest stable release from main branch

Container.Overview: Self-hosted photo browser and organiser. Photos land in a source directory (e.g. via FTP from a camera) and the app automatically sorts them into date folders, generates thumbnails/previews, and serves a web UI for browsing, comparing, flagging, and downloading.
Container.Description: Photo Browser - A self-hosted photo browser and organiser designed for Unraid. Features: automatic date-based sorting, EXIF metadata extraction, RAW file pairing, thumbnail/preview generation, colour flagging, side-by-side and overlay comparison, zoom/pan, and batch ZIP download.

Config.Name: Web UI Port
Config.Description: Port for the Photo Browser web interface.

Config.Name: Photos Directory
Config.Description: Path to your photos. Source photos (e.g. FTP uploads) and sorted date folders live here.

Config.Name: Cache Directory
Config.Description: App data: SQLite database, thumbnail cache, and preview cache. Persist this across updates.

Config.Name: Scan Interval (minutes)
Config.Description: How often the background scanner runs to ingest new photos and repair thumbnails.

Config.Name: Log Level
Config.Description: Logging verbosity: debug, info, warning, error.

Config.Name: Thumbnail Size (px)
Config.Description: Max dimension for grid thumbnails in pixels.

Config.Name: Preview Size (px)
Config.Description: Max dimension for the enlarged preview images in pixels.

Config.Name: Share Download Size (px)
Config.Description: Max dimension for 'Share' quality ZIP downloads.

Config.Name: High Download Size (px)
Config.Description: Max dimension for 'High Quality' ZIP downloads.

Config.Name: Source Directory
Config.Description: Path inside container where new photos arrive (usually same as Photos Directory mount).

Config.Name: Sorted Directory
Config.Description: Path inside container where date-sorted folders are created.

Config.Name: RAW Extensions
Config.Description: Comma-separated list of RAW file extensions to pair with JPEGs.
